lead: you were the emergency contact on a form filled in four years ago by a man you have lunch with twice a year, and the hospital rang you first, and nobody had mentioned it.
sun: the box on that form wants somebody with a solicitor behind them, a spare room, a car that starts on a wet tuesday. you have read that way since your twenties without owning much of it, and the reading needs neither your consent nor your presence, so your name goes down in other people's kitchens, into arrangements settled before it occurred to anyone to check with you.
moon: and there is room. that is what keeps the whole thing running: the space is real, it takes whatever gets set down in it, and nothing about it advertises a limit. eleven people have written you into something. each put in one item, into what was obviously a large amount of space, and each of them is right that one item weighs nothing at all.
pull: eleven people each left one thing with you, each of them certain theirs was the only one, and the pile they have made between them has no name on the outside of it.
tension: the day one of them has to be refused, it will be a single person hearing a single no. the other ten cannot be produced. they were never written down, never agreed to, and reciting them comes out as a comfortable man explaining why a small favour is beyond him. so the refusal lands by itself, on somebody who put your name in a box years ago as a private relief and has not thought about it since.
cost: families that would otherwise have to organise something get to skip the organising, because the gap they were about to notice has your name in it, and the noticing never happens. nobody adds up the pile. the load is entirely aggregate and entirely unwitnessed, every depositor was correct about their own portion, and the sum of it exists in one place only.

lead: she told you in a supermarket aisle, holding a box of something, in the four minutes before her bus, and went home lighter, and you finished the shopping carrying it.
sun: nobody books a room to tell you a thing. standing beside you is apparently private enough by itself, so it arrives in car parks and shop doorways and at the school railings with a child pulling at somebody's sleeve — the worst sentence of a person's decade, handed over sideways, mid-errand, because somebody your size reads as a place rather than as company anyone would have to arrange for.
moon: the taking is not optional. what comes in comes in whole — the sentence, the version underneath it, the year it actually started — and it settles against everything else you have been handed about the same six families in this town. so nobody here gets to be a plain account. you hear the under-track running beneath the ordinary one, in a queue, at a wedding, at a barbecue, permanently.
pull: you were not asked whether you wanted any of it. the telling happens against you the way weather happens against a wall, and they walk off lighter, and you are the room it went into.
tension: saying you are full comes out as a large easy person complaining about being trusted, which sits close enough to ingratitude that it stops in your mouth every time. so it keeps arriving, and the ones bringing it are not being careless — they watched you take the last one with nothing showing afterwards, and read the absence of a mark as a measurement of what it weighed.
cost: somebody can set down the worst hour of their life in four minutes beside a chest freezer and walk off with it lifted, which is rare and which is why it keeps happening to you. what stopped being available is a light conversation. every ordinary exchange here runs over the top of something, you hear both, and the hearing shows on nobody, least of all on you.

lead: there are better players at that table and all of them are keeping time off you, because yours is the one anybody can hear from the door, and a room follows what it can hear.
sun: the tune starts, the ear of the room goes to the largest steady sound available, and that has been you since you were nineteen — so better players tuck in behind a size rather than behind a pair of hands. the arrangement flatters no one in it and has gone unstated for a decade, and it would land as an insult from you and as modesty about you, so it holds.
moon: nothing keeps time on its own. it has to be put out again every week at the same width, whether the week behind it had much in it or not, and the width was never chosen, which is why it has not occurred to anybody that holding it might be work. the pace the table keeps is the pace a large-reading person was assumed to be comfortable at.
pull: the room takes its time off the loudest thing in it. the loudest thing in it did not volunteer, and cannot go quiet for a fortnight without the fortnight becoming an event.
tension: miss two weeks and the account that forms is not that you were busy. it arrives sized to you — a falling-out, an illness, a decision about the whole thing — because nothing about you has ever registered as small, an absence included. so you go on the nights you did not want to go, and the going registers nowhere, since a person who was always there is not doing anything by being there.
cost: for nine years the tune has started on time and nobody has had to count anybody in, which is most of the difference between a session that lasts and one that quietly stops. handing it on is the part that will not work. asking somebody else to hold the beat requires the table to learn that it was being held, and they would hear that as somebody claiming the evening.

lead: you turned to the quiet one at the end and asked what he thought, and he answered, and it was the best thing said all evening, and he has been careful with you ever since.
sun: a room does not hear you stop talking. it hears you hand something over. a gap opened by somebody who reads at that size registers as an allocation instead, and the whole party watches it get made — the man receiving it most of all, who now has an audience he did not have a second earlier and a debt he was not carrying when he sat down.
moon: the opening does not run down. it is not rationed, and the twelfth person of an evening gets it as readily as the first. what goes into it does not come back out. a thing said into that space was said in public, in a room that had just watched the space being cleared for it, and it holds afterwards the way a promise holds.
pull: what he got was somewhere to speak and, in the same second, a clear view of who had arranged for him to have it. the two do not come apart afterwards.
tension: people describe you afterwards as good in a room, or as a natural chair, and neither description can be argued with, because from any seat but yours the opening of a gap and the control of a gap are one movement. getting out of the way at your size is a visible act. so the effort that went into a silence gets filed under command, by people who enjoyed the evening and are being sincere.
cost: quiet people get heard where you are, reliably, and a few of them have not been heard anywhere else in years. the room is standard issue. it goes out to everyone at the same width, so the one who took it as a regard meant particularly for him works out at the next dinner that it was not, and adjusts, and comes less.
